definitions.explanation: Something that was not anticipated or planned for. Became widely known after the 2011 earthquake and nuclear disaster, when officials used this term to describe the scale of the tsunami.

examples.japanese: これは{想定外|そうていがい}の{事態|じたい}だ。
{想定外|そうていがい}の{出来事|できごと}に{対応|たいおう}しなければならない。
examples.english: We must respond to unforeseen events.

examples.japanese: {売|う}り{上|あ}げが{想定外|そうていがい}に{伸|の}びて、{在庫|ざいこ}が{足|た}りなくなった。
examples.english: Sales grew beyond expectations and we ran out of stock.

notes:
USAGE:
Used as a noun or with の as a modifier. Gained widespread public attention after the 2011 Fukushima nuclear disaster, when officials described the magnitude of the tsunami as {想定外|そうていがい}. The term was criticized as an excuse for inadequate preparation. Now commonly used in business and daily life.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {想定外|そうていがい}の{事態|じたい} (unforeseen situation)
- {想定外|そうていがい}の{出来事|できごと} (unexpected event)
- {想定外|そうていがい}の{結果|けっか} (unexpected result)
- {想定外|そうていがい}の{費用|ひよう} (unforeseen costs)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {想定内|そうていない}: within expectations — the opposite, meaning something was anticipated
- {予想外|よそうがい}: unexpected — similar meaning but without the nuance of formal planning
- {想定|そうてい}: assumption, supposition — the base word without the negating {外|がい}
